key_findings.finding: The SMILES is identified in ChEMBL as mesoridazine (CHEMBL1088), an approved compound; the database did not return a specific mechanism-of-action record or direct BBB assay result.

The molecule has a BBB-compatible physicochemical profile: MW 386.59 Da, calculated LogP 4.90, TPSA 29.54 Å², HBD 0, HBA 4, four rotatable bonds, and no Lipinski violations. These values favor passive CNS membrane permeation, although the tertiary amines imply substantial ionization that can reduce the uncharged fraction at physiological pH.

The structure contains two basic tertiary nitrogens: an N-methylpiperidine nitrogen and a ring phenothiazine-like tertiary nitrogen. No explicit pKa/basicity value was provided by the retrieved profile, so ionization and the exact neutral fraction cannot be quantified from the available evidence; the molecule should nevertheless be expected to be predominantly cationic near physiological pH, with some neutral fraction enabling CNS entry.
